title: A string buffer
description:
Write a growable string buffer:

```c
typedef struct { char *data; size_t len; size_t cap; } StrBuf;   /* {0} is a valid empty buffer */

int sb_append(StrBuf *sb, const char *text);          /* 0, or -1 if out of memory */
int sb_appendf(StrBuf *sb, const char *fmt, ...);     /* printf-style; 0 or -1 */
char *sb_take(StrBuf *sb);                            /* hands the string to the caller (never NULL unless out of memory) and resets sb */
void sb_free(StrBuf *sb);                             /* frees and resets */
```

- `data` is always zero-terminated once anything was appended; `len` never counts the zero;
- grow by doubling the capacity (starting at 16), with `realloc` into a temporary;
- `sb_appendf` measures with `vsnprintf(NULL, 0, ...)` first, using `va_copy`;
- `sb_take` on a buffer that never got any text returns a newly allocated empty string.
hints: Put the growing in one `sb_reserve(sb, extra)` helper that makes room for `extra` more characters plus the zero; both appends call it (lesson 8.01).
A `va_list` can only be used once, so `va_copy` it for the measuring call and use the original for the real write.
